# Research Guides: Library Workshop Descriptions: GitHub Portfolios for Job Seekers

## GitHub Portfolios Workshop

Welcome to GitHub Portfolios, a workshop hosted by UO Libraries Data Services and the UO Career Center.

**To participate, please create or sign into your free GitHub account at github.com.** You'll need an email address and we strongly recommend that you set up some sort of two-factor authentication device (such as the Duo app on your phone that you may use to sign in to Duckweb). Here's detailed instructions.

GitHub is a cloud-based platform where you can store, share, and work together with others to write code. It's also a great place to showcase your work to potential employers and collaborators. These instructions from GitHub summarize what we'll over today.

### What makes a good GitHub portfolio?

A simple, professional GitHub portfolio has:

- a professional photograph or icon
- your name
- links to LinkedIn profile, professional website, ORCiD or other professional web presence
- a special repository that has the name of your GitHub username
- this creates a special repository where you can create a README.md page that will show up on the front page of your GitHub
- put in this README a very short introduction and summary of relevant job experience

- add pinned repositories showcasing your coding skills

You can add bells and whistles, but don't need to! Only add things like "GitHub stats" if they make you look good.

#### Step by Step Instructions

- Brainstorm and draft your "about me."
- Create
** **or sign into your free GitHub account at github.com.
- Personalize your GitHub main page by adding information about who you are, a headshot or avatar, and a link to your LinkedIn.
- Create a profile repository and put your About Me text in it. See the first few instructions here. Or read GitHub's documentation here. Here's a list of badges you can add to your About me.
- Make sure your code repositories are documented with a README that explains what it is and how to use it. Ideally, also specify an environment in which to run the code using an environment file.
